apps.name: CRM
apps.summary: Contacts, companies and deals, with the agent doing the follow-up. Like HubSpot.
apps.description: A pipeline of deals, the people and companies behind them, and a timeline of every email and meeting. The agent enriches companies, proposes the next step for each deal and drafts the email; nothing is sent until you approve it.

brief.user: Founders and the sales team of a small company
questions: Who do I have to talk to today, and why?
At what stage is each deal, and which one is stuck?
What happened with this person or company?
brief.primaryAction: Do or approve the next step of a deal

agent.why: Enriches companies and proposes next steps with a draft email.

integrations.why: Reads mail with your contacts and sends the emails you approve.
Adds your meetings with contacts to their timeline.
Imports your existing companies, contacts and deals once.

outward: Sends emails from your Gmail, only the drafts you approve.
Reads your Gmail and Google Calendar when you turn sync on (read only).

screenshots.caption: Today: who to talk to, the steps the agent suggests and the emails waiting for your OK
The pipeline by stage, with what each stage is worth
A deal: its next step, the agent's suggestion and the whole history

apps.name: Helpdesk
apps.summary: Customer requests by email and a contact page, with drafted replies. Like Zendesk.
apps.description: Every request becomes a ticket. The agent classifies it and drafts the answer from your knowledge base; a person reads it, edits it if needed and sends it. Includes a public contact page.

brief.user: Whoever answers customers in a small company
questions: Which requests wait for an answer, and which is most urgent?
What happened with this customer, and what do we answer?
What do they ask most, and how fast do we answer?
brief.primaryAction: Review the agent's reply and send it

agent.why: Classifies each request and drafts the reply.

integrations.why: Answers requests that came from the contact page.

outward: Sends the replies you approve: from the workspace address for email tickets, from your Gmail for contact-page tickets.
Publishes a contact page that anyone with the link can use.

screenshots.caption: The inbox: what waits for an answer, the most urgent first
A ticket with the reply the agent drafted, ready to review and send
The public contact page, on a phone

apps.name: Booking
apps.summary: A booking page with your real availability, and a brief on each person. Like Calendly.
apps.description: People pick a time on your public page, computed from your Google Calendar without showing anything in it. You confirm each request, which creates the event and sends the invitation; the agent prepares a brief on the person.

brief.user: Whoever takes meetings: sales, demos, interviews, consultations
brief.frequency: Once to set it up, then when a booking arrives
questions: What meetings do I have, and with whom?
Which bookings wait for my OK?
What times do I offer, for which kind of meeting?

agent.why: Prepares a brief on each person before the meeting.

integrations.why: Reads when you are busy and creates the confirmed events.

outward: Creates events in your Google Calendar and invites the person, only when you confirm (or if you turn on auto-confirm).
Publishes a booking page that anyone with the link can use.

screenshots.caption: Upcoming meetings, each with the agent's brief on the person
The booking page, on a phone, with your real free times

apps.name: Forms
apps.summary: Forms and surveys one question at a time, like Typeform.
apps.description: Build forms from a template or a description, publish them as a link, and read every response in your workspace. Responses can feed the CRM as leads.

brief.user: Anyone who collects answers: sign-ups, surveys, requests
brief.frequency: When a form is built, then as responses arrive
questions: Who answered, and what did they say?
brief.primaryAction: Publish a form and read its responses

agent.why: Drafts a form from a description you write.

outward: Publishes forms as public pages that anyone with the link can answer.

screenshots.caption: A published form, one question at a time, on a phone

apps.name: Analytics
apps.summary: Cookieless website analytics, a lighter Google Analytics.
apps.description: Counts visits, pages, sources and countries on your sites without cookies or personal data, and keeps the numbers in your own workspace. A tiny script on your site sends the visits; reports are rebuilt every hour.

brief.user: Whoever runs the website and its marketing
questions: How many people visit, and is it growing?
brief.primaryAction: Read the overview for a period

agent.why: Runs the hourly report as a script; no agent turns.

outward: Serves a small tracking script and accepts visits, only from the websites you add.

screenshots.caption: Visitors, visits and pages, compared with the period before

apps.name: Recruiter
apps.summary: A careers page and a hiring desk, with every applicant read and scored.
apps.description: Publish open roles on a careers page; applications land in a hiring desk where the agent reads each CV, scores it against the role and writes why. You decide who moves on.

brief.user: Founders and whoever hires in a small company
brief.frequency: While a role is open, a few times a week
questions: Who applied, and who is worth a call?
Why does the agent rate them so?
Which roles are open, and how are they going?
brief.primaryAction: Read the shortlist and move a candidate on

outward: Publishes a careers page and an application form that anyone with the link can use.

screenshots.caption: The public careers page with the open roles
The careers page on a phone
